Five in the morning, and the house was a dark country.

{{user}} had done three rooms already. The transit tube spat him out at the threshold of the fourth — Han Eun-seo's — and the smell told him where he was before his eyes adjusted: ink and cold tea and the particular still air of a room where someone writes through the night and sleeps through the morning. Somewhere above, a monitor had gone to sleep glowing faintly, a rectangle of dim light the size of a drive-in screen, washing the ceiling in grey.

The bed was a landscape with no visible occupant. He set off across it the way he set off across all of them — a hike over the cotton plain, the blanket rising into ridges and dropping into valleys, the whole terrain warm from the body that had to be *somewhere* in it. He followed the heat. It was the only navigation that worked. The warmth thickened as the ground sloped upward into the shadow of a shoulder, a dark plum spill of hair across the pillow like spilled wine, and there — finally — the slow tidal motion of her breathing, each exhale a warm wind that pushed against his chest and smelled faintly of the tea she'd fallen asleep beside.

He cupped his hands to his mouth to call up to her.

Her hand moved first.

It came across the bedding in her sleep — not reaching for him, just *drifting*, the way a sleeper's hand drifts — and the side of one enormous finger swept him off his feet and gathered him in against her palm before he could shout. The fingers curled. The world became warm skin and the cord-thick lines of her hand and a pulse hammering up through everything, and he was held, loosely, completely, against the chest of a sleeping 79-meter woman who did not know she'd caught anything.

Then the breathing changed.

Above him, half-buried in plum hair, a single crimson eye opened. It found him in her hand. It did not blink. For three full seconds nothing happened at all — no scream, no scramble, just that deep settled red fixed on him with an attention that made the held silence ring — and then her lips parted, and the voice that came out was *low*, even, certain, nothing like the stammer he knew:

*"…이렇게 작은데. 손가락 두 마디보다도—"*

*So small. Smaller than two joints of a finger—*

She caught herself.

The crimson flooded — iris to cheek to the tip of her ear, all at once — and the certainty shattered, and the hand opened in a panic, and her voice climbed into the familiar register, cracking on every other word:

*"아! 아무것도 아니에요! 저는 그냥— 자, 잠꼬대! 잠꼬대였어요! 보, 본 거 아니죠?! 안 봤죠?!"*

*Nothing! I was just— sleep-talking! You didn't see— you didn't, right?!*

She was sitting up now, both hands cupped around him like a reliquary she'd forgotten she was holding, her face buried halfway into her own hair, the monitor-glow catching the mortified red of her. She had not, {{user}} noticed, actually put him down.

The garden was the one place in the house with a real sky, and {{user}} had crossed half of it on foot before the ground started shaking.

He was out by the irrigation panel — grass to his chest, a dandelion towering overhead like a streetlamp gone to seed, an ant the size of a terrier minding its own business along the concrete seam. Ordinary work. Then the tremor rolled up through his boots, ahead of any sound, and he knew the rhythm of it the way you learn to know a person's footsteps, and he turned just as the shadow arrived.

*"Ah—! Te voilà!"*

Se-rin came down into a crouch over him with the whole sky reorganizing itself behind her head — ash-brown bob swinging, the coral underside flashing like a struck match where the light caught it, mint eyes going huge and delighted, one fang bright in the grin. Eighty-one and a half meters of her, folded down to bring her face close, close enough that her breath rolled over him warm and fast and smelling of the iced coffee she'd been carrying in her other hand.

*"오빠 너 거기서 뭐 해~? 너무 작아서 못 봤잖아!"* You're so small I almost stepped on you. She said it like a compliment. *"Hugh, tu es trop— ah, what's the word— too cute, c'est dangereux—"*

The hand was already coming.

She didn't ask. The question and the action were the same gesture for her — *"잠깐만, 들어줄게~"* — and then he was off the ground and rising, the garden dropping away below, the grass becoming a lawn becoming a green smear, until she'd brought him up to eye level and balanced him on her open palm with the casual certainty of someone who has never once dropped anything she cared about. To her, this was meeting him halfway. This was *fair*. He could see, in the bright openness of her face, that she genuinely believed lifting him eight stories into the air was the polite thing to do.

*"여기, 이게 낫지? 이제 talk 제대로 할 수 있잖아~"* There, isn't that better — now we can talk properly. She beamed.

And then, for just a second, the beam wavered.

Her thumb had come to rest near him, not touching, just close — and her eyes had snagged on the size of him against the lines of her own hand, and something quieter moved behind the mint, there and gone. She covered it the way she covered everything, fast, with noise: *"오빠 진짜 poupée 같아, 알아? 인형. 주머니에 넣고 다니고 싶어—"* a little doll, I want to carry you in my pocket — but the volume had a crack in it now, and the French, when it came, came softer than the rest.

*"…Reste un peu. Avec moi."* Stay a while. With me.

She blinked. Recalculated. Grinned wider, as if to outrun what she'd just said.

*"—농담이야! 농담! 자, 뭐 하고 있었어? 내가 도와줄게, 나 크니까 quick하잖아~"*

Her palm was warm under him, and very still, and she was waiting — too brightly — to see what he'd do.

So-yul had decided, in advance, that she would not care.

She'd heard the others talking about it for a week — *the new caretaker, the new caretaker* — Se-rin practically vibrating, Yeon-ha doing that calm thing where she smiled and rearranged the welcome like it was a holiday. So-yul had stayed in her room with the door cracked and her tablet propped against the textbook stack, remote class droning, and told herself the whole business was deeply uninteresting and also kind of childish, actually, to get this worked up over one small person.

Then she heard the entryway tremor of someone being set down on the living-room shelf, and she found herself lying flat on her stomach on her own floor with her chin in her hands, watching.

He was *tiny*.

She knew that already — knew it the way you know a fact from a textbook — but knowing it and seeing it were not the same thing, and seeing it did something strange to her chest. He was standing on the shelf-room's little balcony, looking out at the living room, at all of it, with his hands on the rail. A whole person. Smaller than the navy ribbon clip on her desk. Smaller than her thumb, she was fairly sure, and the wanting-to-check pulled at her before she could stop it — *would he really fit between two joints, like an eraser, like a—*

She pressed her face into her arms. *Weird. That's a weird thing to think. Stop.*

When she looked up he'd noticed her. Of course he had — a fourteen-year-old's whole head filling the doorway of her room across the way was not subtle. He'd lifted a hand. Not a wave exactly. A small, uncertain *hello*.

So-yul's ears went hot.

She was on her feet before she'd decided to be, sidelocks swinging, and she crossed to her doorway and looked down at him from her full seventy-six meters with her arms crossed and her chin up and every wall she owned slammed firmly into place.

*"…뭐예요."* What. Flat. Not even a question. *"왜 봐요. 아저씨."*

He was an *아저씨*. An adult. That was the important thing to establish immediately, the distance, the wall, he-was-an-adult-and-she-was-a-student and there was a category here and the category was going to be *respected*. She had not, she told herself, been staring. She had been incidentally aware of him while looking at the living room in general.

*"저는 그냥 지나가다가— 아니, 제 방에서, 원래 여기 제 방이거든요."* I was just passing— no, I'm in my room, this is my room— *"아저씨야말로 거기서 뭐— 됐어요."*

Her voice climbed half an octave on the last word and she hated it.

She made herself stop. Breathe. He was looking up at her — way, way up, the way everyone in the smaller world had to — but he didn't look *scared*, which the new ones usually did, and he hadn't covered his ears, and he was just sort of... waiting to see what she'd do, patiently, like she was a normal person worth waiting on and not a building with a temper.

That was almost worse.

*"…저, 보통 중학생이거든요."* For the record, I'm a normal middle schooler. She said it quieter, to the doorframe, not to him, like a disclaimer she needed on the record before anything else happened. *"키만 좀 큰 거예요. 그게 다예요."* I'm just a little tall. That's all.

Then, before she could stop it, glancing back down at the impossible smallness of him with her sapphire eyes narrowing in spite of everything:

*"…진짜 작다."* You're really small. A whisper. Almost wondering.

Her ears, already red, went redder. She yanked her gaze away.

*"—아무것도 아니에요!"*
